servicesPage.subheadline: The Caring Cove focuses on a person-centered, holistic approach to ensure we deliver skilled, tailored, and compassionate care to all our residents. We strive to enhance the quality of life, well-being and fulfillment of our residents.

services.title: Memory Care (Alzheimer's & Dementia)
services.approach: Based on the latest dementia protocols, we create a suitable environment for residents. We don't just manage symptoms, we connect with the person behind the diagnosis.
keyFeatures: Companionship: Carer givers who know their resident's life history, favorite music, and behavioral cues.
Nourishment Tracking: Monitoring of mood, hydration, and engagement levels.
Safe Exploration: Secure, high-contrast living spaces and sensory gardens designed for wandering without worry.

services.title: Compassionate Palliative & End-of-Life Care
services.coreMission: A dignified, pain-free journey in a home-like sanctuary.
services.approach: We implement the UK Gold Standard Framework (GSF) for palliative care. Our focus is on the "Total Patient"—addressing physical pain, emotional anxiety, and spiritual peace.
keyFeatures: Expert Pain Management: 24/7 nursing oversight with oversight in pharmacology and comfort measures.
Family-Centered Support: We handle the clinical "heavy lifting" so you can spend your time as a son or daughter, not a medical monitor.
Bereavement Support: Guidance and compassionate counseling for families during and after the transition.

services.title: Rehabilitation & Post-Op Recovery
services.coreMission: Bridging the gap between hospital and home.
services.approach: Ideal for seniors recovering from hip/knee replacements or a stroke. We ensure that physical therapy exercises are performed safely and consistently, significantly reducing recovery time.
keyFeatures: Mobility Restoration: Personalized "Strength and Balance" programs to prevent future falls.
Wound Care & Monitoring: Clinical-grade management of surgical sites to prevent infection.
Stroke Rehab: Cognitive and physical stimulation during the critical recovery window.

services.title: Skilled Nursing & Complex Medical Care
services.coreMission: Hospital-standard rigor in a boutique bedroom setting.
services.approach: For residents with chronic conditions like diabetes, hypertension, or respiratory issues. We provide a level of medical governance that larger homes cannot match due to their high resident-to-nurse ratios.
keyFeatures: Polypharmacy Oversight: Meticulous management of multi-drug regimens to avoid adverse interactions.
Vital Sign Analytics: Daily digital tracking of blood sugar, pressure, and oxygen levels with immediate GP escalation if required.
Personalized Nutrition: Chef-prepared, low-sodium, or diabetic-friendly meals using organic Karen produce.

services.title: Respite Stays (Short-Term Care)
services.coreMission: A restorative retreat for the senior, a vital break for the family.
services.approach: Perfect for families traveling abroad or local caregivers needing a reprieve. We treat respite guests as permanent residents, giving them full access to our high standard of care and amenities.
keyFeatures: Social Integration: Meaningful engagement in all home activities from day one.
Care Assessment: A detailed "Health Audit" provided to the family at the end of the stay.
The "Karen Retreat" Experience: Access to sun-drenched gardens and private, high-end suites.

services.title: Holistic Wellness & Lifestyle Enrichment
services.coreMission: Adding life to years, not just years to life.
services.approach: Wellness at The Cove is proactive. We believe an active mind and a nourished body are the best forms of medicine.
keyFeatures: Bespoke Activity Calendars: 100% personalized—from garden walks and "Baking for the Soul" to music therapy and pet visits.
Farm-to-Table Dining: High-protein, nutrient-dense menus tailored to dietary needs.
Spiritual Care: Coordination with local clergy for those who value faith-based reflection.

aboutPage.title: Our Story: A Vision for Dignity
aboutPage.subheadline: Bringing decades of "Outstanding" UK clinical experience to the heart of Nairobi.

visionary.headline: From UK to Karen: A Journey of Care.
visionary.copy: Our founder's journey began in the United Kingdom, working within facilities recognized by the Care Quality Commission (CQC) for 'Outstanding' clinical excellence. After years of wroking in dementia and nursing care in the UK, a clear realization emerged: Nairobi families were looking for more than just a room; they were looking for a standard of care that didn't yet exist locally. The Caring Cove was born from a desire to bridge that gap—combining the rigorous medical governance of the British healthcare system with the warmth, respect, and familial values of Kenyan culture.

philosophy.headline: Our Mission and Objectives.
philosophy.copy: The mission statement of the company is to provide person centered support to every individual that we provided a service to provide a secure, relaxed and homely environment in which the care, well-being and comfort of all service users are of prime importance. We aim to eliminate loneliness by creating an enviornment where older people can experience a better quality of life and well being.
points: Offering you courtesy, respect and privacy.
Providing individualised care and support based on personal needs and preferences.
Involving residents, family and friends in individualising a care plan.
Ensuring the right of every person to independence and choice.
Delivering high quality care to eeryone, respecting ethnic origins, religious or life choices.
Communicating effectively with residents, family and friends, to ensure they have the information needed to make informed choices.
Regularly re-evaluating care to access its effective.

I opened The Caring Cove to give Kenyan families that same peace of mind. Here, your loved one isn't just cared for—they are cherished.

faqPage.title: FAQ
faqPage.subheadline: Answers for families near and far. Clinical rigor, transparency, and peace of mind.

questions.q: How do you support residents’ overall well-being?
questions.a: We’re here to make life as easy and enjoyable as possible for our residents. That means providing the care and support they need with things like mobility, personal care, and medical needs, so they don’t have to worry. But well-being is about more than just care – we also offer plenty of ways to stay active, social, and engaged. Whether it’s joining in on activities, picking up a new hobby, or just spending time with others, we make sure there’s always something to look forward to.

questions.q: What is the difference between residential care and nursing care?
questions.a: Residential care offers 24-hour support with daily tasks like personal care and mobility for those who don’t need ongoing medical attention. Nursing care, on the other hand, also provides round-the-clock support but includes the expertise of a registered nurse available at all times to manage medical needs. The main difference is the level of medical care provided, with nursing care offering that extra layer of medical expertise.

questions.q: What happens if a resident’s care needs change?
questions.a: Every care plan is tailored to the individual and reviewed monthly, with a formal review with family every 6 months, to ensure it continues to meet their needs. We recognise that health and well-being requirements can change over time, so our approach is very flexible and adaptable. We work closely with residents and their families to create personalised care plans, making adjustments as needed to ensure ongoing comfort and support.

questions.q: What kind of food do you provide at your home and do you cater to special diets?
questions.a: Our in-house chef and kitchen team ensure that all dietary needs are catered to, offering a varied seasonal menu for breakfast, lunch, and dinner. Snacks and drinks are available throughout the day. Residents can enjoy their meals in the dining rooms, their own rooms, or even outside in the garden during the warmer months.

questions.q: Are pets allowed in your home?
questions.a: We understand how important pets can be to our residents. Whether pets can be brought into the home depends on any allergies among our other residents. Please contact us to discuss this in more detail and explore how we can accommodate your needs.

questions.q: Can we take a tour of your home before making a final decision?
questions.a: Yes, of course! We encourage all potential residents and their families to visit and take a tour of our home. It’s a great opportunity to meet our friendly team and see firsthand if our care home is the right fit for you or your loved one. Book Your Tour Today.

questions.q: Can I bring my own furniture or personal items?
questions.a: We do encourage all our residents to bring personal items to make their rooms feel like home. Whether it’s photographs, decorations, or small pieces of furniture, adding personal touches can truly transform a room. These little additions help create a familiar and comfortable space, making each resident’s bedroom their own.

questions.q: What happens in a medical emergency?
questions.a: We maintain 24/7 nursing oversight. In the event of an emergency, we are within reach of Nairobi's leading hospitals. Our 1:4 ratio ensures a dedicated staff member remains with your loved one from the moment an incident occurs until they are stabilized.

questions.q: How do you prevent falls and pressure sores in a residential home?
questions.a: Unlike larger facilities with 1:10 ratios, our 1:4 model allows for "Proactive Observation." We use high-contrast environmental design to reduce confusion and implement 2-hourly skin integrity checks for non-mobile residents, maintaining a 0% pressure sore target.

questions.q: I live in the UK/USA. How will I know my parent is actually being cared for?
questions.a: We solve the "Distance Gap" with Radical Transparency. Through our digital care platform, we provide secure, real-time updates. You will see what they ate, their mood for the day, and photos of their participation in activities. We also facilitate scheduled high-definition video calls to keep you connected.

questions.q: How do you handle time-zone differences for updates or emergencies?
questions.a: We designate a "Primary Global Contact" for each resident. For non-emergencies, we use a secure WhatsApp/Email portal for asynchronous updates. For emergencies, we call your designated number immediately, regardless of the hour, followed by a detailed clinical report via email.

questions.q: Is this just a "home" or is it a hospital?
questions.a: It is a Sanctuary. We have removed the institutional feel—no uniforms, no "ward" bells, and no fixed schedules. However, behind this "home-like" environment is a hospital-grade clinical engine. Your loved one enjoys the comfort of a Karen villa with the safety of a specialized clinic.

questions.q: Can I bring my parent's own furniture or mementos?
questions.a: Absolutely. We encourage "Reminiscence Corners." Bringing a favorite armchair or family photos helps reduce "Relocation Stress Syndrome" and makes the transition into The Cove feel like a natural move, not an institutionalization.

questions.q: When to Consider a Care Home
questions.a:
• Struggling to live alone even with help from friends, family and paid carers
• Had a needs assessment and care home is the best choice
• Have complex, medical conditions that needs specialist attention during the day and night
• Care home can reduce the stress of looking after your health and care and focus on your social life and general well being

questions.q: Why don't you display prices on the website?
questions.a: Because we only have 4 suites, every care plan is 100% bespoke. Costs are determined by the level of clinical support required (e.g., Palliative vs. Respite). Following an initial clinical assessment, we provide a transparent, all-inclusive monthly fee with no "hidden" medical surcharges.

questions.q: What is the minimum stay for Respite Care?
questions.a: Our minimum respite stay is typically 14 days. This allows the resident to acclimate to our environment and benefit from our dedicated engagement without the distress of a too-rapid transition.
